subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should the read tool get a narrow binary-document fallback now, or should this issue wait for broader document parsing/provider-native file work?
rationale: Current source still has the token-waste behavior, but related issues propose richer extraction and provider-native forwarding, and the only open narrow implementation candidate is conflicting.

options.title: Land narrow fallback
options.body: Review, repair, or replace the linked guard PR so known PDF/Office reads return a clear fallback message instead of decoded bytes.

options.title: Fold into broader document work
options.body: Keep this issue as context for provider-native file/document architecture and close the conflicting guard PR without a narrow read-tool change.

options.title: Implement parser-backed read extraction
options.body: Allow `read` to extract document text directly, but require explicit security and ownership review for ZIP/XML parsing and dependency boundaries first.

recommendation.title: Land narrow fallback
recommendation.body: Review, repair, or replace the linked guard PR so known PDF/Office reads return a clear fallback message instead of decoded bytes.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal for the read-wrapper ownership boundary is steipete's prior split of the read tool surface.
